notes.key_insight: at batch-1 decode only top-8 of 64 experts are read per layer, so the memory floor is the ACTIVE weights (~1.3B, 2.36 GB) not the 6.9B total. floor = 2.339 ms.
notes.fused_recipe: reuses the dense Part-1 kernels (rmsnorm+QKV GEMV, split-K flash-decode, o-proj GEMV) plus MoE-specific kernels: QK-norm+RoPE+cache-write fused, router GEMV, indirect-indexed expert SwiGLU (grid top_k x I-tiles, gathers gate_up_proj[e] by GPU-tensor id), gated expert-down+residual combine. whole step CUDA-graph-captured; data-dependent expert ids live in a static GPU tensor overwritten each step, so routing changes token-to-token but the launch stays shape-stable. torch glue = 2 QK-norm scale reductions + router softmax/topk per layer.
notes.verified: argmax-identical to hand-rolled torch oracle (itself 12/12 vs HF) over 12 real greedy-decode steps.
notes.result: beat vLLM 3.698 -> 3.283 (1.13x faster, 305 vs 270 tok/s), 1.40x the 2.339ms active floor. same playbook as the dense megakernel, now sparse.
